rationale:
Issue #910 reports that Int64.operator== throws an exception when comparing with non-Int64/int/Int32 types (e.g., Object, null) due to the _promote helper attempting unsafe casts. The minimized production patch replaces the problematic `_i == _promote(other)` with explicit type checks that return false for unsupported types, eliminating the exception. The trigger test 'test/int64_test.dart::==' was rewritten in the fixing commit to test operator== directly rather than through the equals matcher (which was hiding the exceptions), making the test semantically equivalent to the reported defect. All strict runtime gates passed: buggy version reproduces only the declared trigger deterministically (3 repetitions), fixed version passes all tests, and the patch contains only the operator== logic change with no refactoring, formatting, or unrelated modifications. No active same-project root causes exist to duplicate against.

Issue #910 reports that Int64.operator== throws an exception when comparing with unrelated types due to _promote() helper attempting type conversion. The minimized production patch replaces the single-line _promote() implementation with explicit type checks that return false for unrelated types. The trigger test 'test/int64_test.dart::==' was rewritten in the fixing commit from using the 'equals' matcher (which silently catches exceptions as false) to direct == assertions, exposing the actual exception behavior. This is semantically equivalent - both test the same equality operations, but the later version correctly fails on the buggy code instead of masking the exception. The minimized patch is identical to production-fix.patch and contains only the operator== logic change with no refactoring, formatting, or unrelated changes. All strict runtime checks passed with deterministic reproduction (3 fingerprint groups). No active duplicates exist in the same project.
